msContents.summary:
[p]Written in a rounded gothic hand, 36/37 lines to a page. Some headings in red, and some capitals and paragraph marks in alternate red-blue, blue-red.[/p] [p][b]Contents[/b][/p]
[p]1. f. 1r [i]Precatio terrae matris[/i], abbreviated and corrupted[/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Dea sancta tellus regenerationis per que [sic] de cuncta gerensa [sic] generasti...'
[p]Explicit: '...hoc michi es quod te suplex rogo'.[/p]
[p]2. ff. 1r-3v [i]Precatio omnium herbarum[/i], abbreviated and corrupted[/p]
[p]Incipit: 'V[o]s potestates omnes herbas. Or[o] [e]xoro magestatemque [sic] uos quas parens tellus...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...attussicos. Cxxxvi.'[/p]
[p]3. ff. 3v-6r Antonius Musa, [i]De herba vettonica[/i][/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Caesari augusto prestantissimo...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...mire dolorem lenire experti afirmant'.[/p]
[p]4. ff. 6v-37r Pseudo-Apuleius, [i]Herbarius[/i][/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Paucas uires herbarum et curationes corporis...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: 'Herbarium apulei platonici quem [sic] accept a chironi. Macistro Achilis. Et Ascolapio. Explicit feliciter.'[/p]
[p]5. ff. 37v-38v Anonymous, [i]De taxone[/i][/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Non modo studiosus set etiam capecem mutuo inter uos congnouissem marcelline...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...et modice subsiccet et initiat sibi in cor pur [sic] purgabitur'.[/p]
[p]6. ff. 38v-46v and 76r-149v Sextus Placitus, [i]De medicina ex animalibus[/i][/p]
[p]Incipit (f. 39r) 'De cervo et ad omnes homines cornus ceruinus habetuim...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: 'Explicit liber de uirtutibus herbarum peccudum et quorundam alliorum animalium etc.'.[/p]
[p]7. ff. 46v-68v [i]'Curae herbarum[/i], interpolated within the Sextus Placitus herbal[/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Nomen herbe licanis stefanotice. Folia habet oblonga...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: 'Paralyticus enim eam tonsam herbam cum lac bubulum et storacem calamitem statim eum liberabit. Expliciunt cure herbarum feliciter.'[/p]
[p]8. ff. 68v-75r Receipts, interpolated within Sextus Placitus herbal[/p]
[p]Begins: 'Ad cauculum de perna uteri quod appelatur uertebra...'[/p]
[p]Ends: '...ad distilationem [sic] urine'.[/p]
[p]9. ff. 150r-151r Relation of a cure of a friend of the scribe[/p]
[p]Begins: 'Conquestus est michi G. abustusus religiosus qui erat amicus meus...'.[/p]
[p]10. ff. 151v-152v Tables of Roman and Arabic numerals from 1 to 1,000,000.[/p]
[p]Initials: On fol. 1 are two illuminated historiated initials. The first a D, showing a seated bearded figure in a purple robe and blue over-dress, holding a red book [Hippocrates? Asklepius?]: below this another similar initial U showing three plants in a bowl [?]. In the upper corners, one on each side, a Sun and a Moon. On fol. 75v is a full page illustration in colours of three standing male figures, one of which is a nude boy: they appear on a filed of flowers, with three trees in the background. Charles Singer has suggested that this is probably a Christian version of the Presentation to Apuleius of the 'Herbarius' by Aesculapius and Chiron.[/p]
[p]The MS. is illustrated by 159 coloured, and 44 uncoloured drawings of plants and animals. In a few cases there are blank spaces where the illustrations have been omitted.[/p]
[p][b]Bibliography[/b][/p]
[p]Clark, Willene B. and McMunn, Meradith T. [i]Beasts and birds of the Middle Ages: the bestiary and its legacy[/i] (Philadelphia: University of Pennsylvania Press, 1989), p. 573.[/p]
[p]Collins, Minta. [i]Medieval Herbals: The Illustrative Traditions[/i] (Toronto: University of Toronto Press, 2000), pp. 156-162, [i]et passim[/i][p]
[p]Kristeller, Paul Oskar; Cranz, Ferdinand Edward and Brown, Virginia. [i]Mediaeval and Renaissance Latin Translations and Commentaries[/i], vols. 4-5 (Washington DC: Catholic University of America Press, 1980), p. 128[/p]

history.provenance: [p]Owned in the 17th century by Marco Cremosano (1611-1704), historian and antiquarian from Milan, Italy, his ownershipt note 'Marci Cremosani' in black ink on upper flyleaf.[/p]
history.acquisition: Purchased at a Hoepli Sale at Milan 13 June 1930, Lot 143.
